name: The Game Extension
author: unknown

provenance.from: Ultimate Amiga forum, AMOS Factory downloads section, retrieved 2026-07-26. Most items there are credited "provided and archived by Lonewolf10". Archive path: tge_beta.
provenance.note: Documentation coverage is counted as keywords with a dedicated node in TGE.guide.beta: 61 of 103. An earlier figure of 73 came from a looser measure -- how many of the library's own keyword names appear anywhere in the files shipped beside it -- which counts a name mentioned in passing as documentation. Neither figure is the usable total: three of the 61 nodes read only "Removed", so 58 describe a keyword at all, and two more ("NOT DONE", "dont use") describe one the author had abandoned. Coverage does not set the evidence tier, which follows from what is available to read.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified unless stated in the notes. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

notes: A game-oriented toolkit -- 103 keywords covering CD32 pads, requesters, vertical blank and mouse handling. It is a SHIM over other people's libraries, not a self-contained extension: the binary opens req, reqtools, lowlevel, ptreplay, stc, amos, graphics, dos, icon and workbench, plus GMS's dpkernel.library, which the guide confirms -- "TGE uses GMS, and so you must pay all according gms lisences, and your program will require gms(if you use TGE gfx)". Sixty-one of the 103 have a dedicated node in TGE.guide.beta. THE GUIDE LAGS THE TABLE AND CANNOT BE PORTED FROM. Six of its nodes name keywords the table does not have: `G Getbob` and `A=G Pixel` are earlier names for `g get img` and `g point`, `G Encyrpt` and `G Decyrpt` misspell `g encrypt` and `g decrypt` (while the table's own `g init encyrpt` misspells it the same way and must stay misspelled, being what programs tokenise against), `G Set Raster` says "NOT done yet." and never shipped, and `A=G Open Req` says "Removed". The requester group is the clearest case: the guide marks all four of `A=G Open Req`, `G Close Req`, `A=G Open Reqtools` and `G Close Reqtools` "Removed", yet three of them are still in the table with live routines. Reading those routines settles it -- routine 9 opens the library named at the workspace's +32 ("reqtools.library") and stores its base at +28, routine 10 closes it, and routine 8 closes a base at +12 that NOTHING in the code hunk ever writes. The string "req.library" is still at +16 with no reference to it anywhere. So req support really was removed and its closer was left behind calling CloseLibrary on a permanently zero pointer. Two more the guide flags and the binary confirms: `g agaplasma` is documented "NOT DONE" and its routine 41 is a bare rts, and `g set mouse` is documented "DONT USE" and its routine 80 writes two overlapping longs -- `move.l d0,2868(a0)` then `move.l d1,2866(a0)`, so the second store clobbers half of the first. The table's 107 entries are one null entry, 103 named keywords and three argument variants: `!g plot`, `!g iconify` and `!g line` each end their spec with $FE instead of $FF and are followed by an empty-named entry carrying the alternate spec and its own routine. That convention holds across the whole registry -- 456 names begin with `!` over 72 tables and 455 are followed by an empty-named entry, the one exception being intuition-1.3b's `!ipoint`. NOTE: the binary embeds the string "Do NOT Distrubte" [sic] beside its version cookie, which reflects its 1998 shareware terms and not a bar on writing a compatible player. Andrew Burton's AMOS Extensions List (kept at ultimateamiga.com, updated 2007-07-29), compiled from the AMOS-LIST archives 1994-1998, Amiga magazine clippings and coverdisk CDs. records version 0.4b; the binary's own $VER says 0.9, and the binary is taken as authoritative.
